registration.question: Between genes, where no rule can name the gene whose body the element sits in, does the gene with the nearest 5' end inside the element's boundary-delimited domain match the element's own cell type more often than the gene with the nearest 5' end on the arm? Section 9 could not ask it: on Calderon et al. 2022's 917 between-gene elements the two rules named the same gene for all but 90, under the stop rule's 200. This lane's counts show that no measured boundary set reaches 200 on that population at any density, so the source changes, not the boundary set.
registration.route: route (b) of section 9's 'what follows': a source with more between-gene elements. Route (a), a 6-16 h boundary set, is closed by the counts in this registration's inventory.
registration.element_source: Janssens J, Aibar S, Taskiran II, et al. (2022) Decoding gene regulation in the fly brain. Nature 601:630-636, doi:10.1038/s41586-021-04262-z; the authors' differentially accessible region table (tbl_DARs.txt) and cell-type table (cellTypeInfo.tsv) from flybrain.aertslab.org; GEO GSE163697 holds the reads
registration.element_licence: not stated: the article is subscription-only (Europe PMC records no licence and no PMCID) and the data portal flybrain.aertslab.org states no licence, no terms of use and no copyright line; the GEO record states no terms either. Recorded, not inferred. This is the same standing as Calderon et al. 2022, which lane-fly used and recorded the same way (section 8)

boundary_set.primary: Stadler, Haines, Eisen 2017 (eLife 6:e29550, CC BY 4.0), supplementary file 1, Table S4: the authors' manual call on nuclear-cycle-14 embryos at 500-bp resolution, dm6 as given. lane-flynode's set, carried unchanged (registration f5985f7)
boundary_set.why_unchanged: only the element source changes here, so a disagreement with section 9 is attributable to the source and not to the boundaries as well; this is simpler_fly.py's own reason (section 8 item 1) applied the other way round
beside_deciding_nothing: Dolsten et al. 2025 (Cell Genomics 5:101002, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0), Table S2: 3,521 boundary spans of a Micro-C atlas covering nc1-8, nc14 and stages 10-12 (about 6-8 h), 800-bp spans at 400-bp insulation bins, Release 6. Its text states 3,673 boundaries and the shipped sheet holds 3,521 rows; the sheet is used as shipped and the difference is noted
Kaushal et al. 2022 (Sci Adv 8:eabl8834, CC BY 4.0), data file S2: the 2,334 2-kb bins the authors mark `exist.WT_0` in wild-type 2-6 h embryos, dm6

Kaushal et al. 2021 (Nat Commun 12:1011, CC BY 4.0), supplementary data 3: the 3,458 2-kb bins the authors mark `exist.wildtype` in wild-type third-instar larval central nervous system, dm6. This is the only set whose TISSUE matches the elements', and it is beside rather than primary only because the primary set is carried from f5985f7 unchanged; it is the obvious primary of a next registration
boundary_set.stage: the primary boundaries come from 2-3 h embryos while the elements and the RNA come from larval-to-adult brain. That is a WIDER stage gap than section 9's, not a narrower one, and it is the price of a population large enough to ask the question. It is stated in the reading, it is not tested here, and the larval-CNS set reported beside is the one whose tissue matches

registration.node: simpler_flynode's boundary rule, unchanged but for each set's own bin: an element's domain runs from the boundary at or left of its midpoint to the next boundary right of it, or to the arm end; a gene is in the domain when its 5' end lies there or inside either boundary's bin; the rule names the in-domain gene with the nearest 5' end, and falls back to nearest TSS when the domain holds no 5' end
registration.population: the between-gene elements: regions Janssens et al. 2022 calls differentially accessible UP, at cluster resolution lvl1 against the rest of the whole brain, in EXACTLY one of the 42 RNA clusters its own cellTypeInfo.tsv declares a counterpart for, whose midpoint lies more than 1 kb from any transcript 5' end and in no protein-coding gene body
registration.endpoint: simpler_fly's, unchanged: the attributed gene is counted concordant when it reaches 5 counts per million in the element's own label and is higher there than in every other label, in RNA summed over that label's cells. A gene absent from the RNA atlas's rows is not concordant, and the number of such genes is reported
registration.outcome: the boundary rule against nearest TSS on the between-gene elements; percentile cluster bootstrap over 1-Mb windows; BOUNDARY_RULE_AHEAD, NEAREST_AHEAD or NO_DIFFERENCE_DETECTED
registration.second_registered_comparison: the boundary rule against the worm's gene-structure rule on the same elements, with its own label, not the outcome. Two comparisons on one population, each at 95%, no correction
registration.matched_control_and_falsifier: simpler_fly's matched-distance control applied to the boundary rule's gene on the population: FALSIFIED when the rule's genes match the element's label no more often than genes drawn at a matched distance (one-sided p >= 0.05)
registration.positive_control: simpler_fly's: nearest TSS on the promoter elements (within 500 bp of a 5' end) against its own matched control. If it does not separate, the readout is declared unresponsive and the primary reading is withheld
beside_deciding_nothing: the same boundaries rotated along each arm by one uniform offset, number and spacing kept, 1,000 draws
the two other measured boundary sets on the same elements
the elements where the two rules differ, alone
all distal elements, and the gene-structure rule against nearest TSS
labels holding 50 or more population elements
registration.power_in_advance: 216 of 3,265 population elements differ under the primary boundary set: about 1.3 points at 80% power, two-sided 5%, before clustering, against the 2.9 points section 9 could bound on its 90
registration.stop_rule: one run; fewer than 200 differing between-gene elements stops it unscored. The census counts 216 under the primary set and, beside, 209 under Dolsten 2025, 174 under Kaushal 2021's larval CNS and 162 under Kaushal 2022. Only the primary set and Dolsten 2025 reach 200, so the two sets reported beside that do not are read as beside and nothing else
registration.money: none; no model request, no key read

outcome_wording.head: On {n} D. melanogaster brain distal elements called differentially accessible in exactly one of {t} cell types (Janssens et al. 2022, larval to adult brain, the source's own lvl1 call against the rest of the brain) and lying in no protein-coding gene body, the gene with the nearest 5' end inside the element's domain, delimited by {nb} Hi-C boundaries of nuclear-cycle-14 embryos (Stadler et al. 2017, the authors' manual call), is expressed at 5 counts per million or more and highest in the element's own cell type, in RNA summed over that cell type's cells (Davie et al. 2018, the counterpart cluster the accessibility source itself declares), for {kb} of {n} ({cb}%), against {kn} of {n} ({cn}%) for the gene with the nearest 5' end on the arm; the rules differ on {k} of {n} elements; difference {d} points, 95% {lo} to {hi} over 1-Mb clusters.
outcome_wording.BOUNDARY_RULE_AHEAD: On this endpoint the boundary rule is ahead of nearest TSS.
outcome_wording.NEAREST_AHEAD: On this endpoint nearest TSS is ahead of the boundary rule.
outcome_wording.NO_DIFFERENCE_DETECTED: No difference detected between the boundary rule and nearest TSS.
outcome_wording.meaning_BOUNDARY_RULE_AHEAD: No rule names a host gene on this population, so the lead does not come from the element sitting inside the named gene's transcribed body, which is what section 8 could not rule out and section 9 had too few elements to ask.
outcome_wording.meaning_NEAREST_AHEAD: Where the nearest 5' end lies across a measured boundary, the gene across it matches the element's cell type more often than the gene inside the domain.
outcome_wording.meaning_NO_DIFFERENCE_DETECTED: With {k} elements differing, a difference smaller than about {mde} points could go undetected; section 9 could only bound it at 2.9 points, on {fly} differing elements.
outcome_wording.gene_structure: Against the gene-structure rule on the same elements ({kg} of {n}, {cg}%; the two differ on {k2}, and neither names a host here), the difference is {d2} points, 95% {lo2} to {hi2}:
outcome_wording.gene_structure_BOUNDARY_RULE_AHEAD: the boundary rule is ahead of the gene-structure rule.
outcome_wording.gene_structure_GENE_STRUCTURE_AHEAD: the gene-structure rule is ahead of the boundary rule.
outcome_wording.gene_structure_NO_DIFFERENCE_DETECTED: no difference detected between the two nodes.
outcome_wording.NOT_FALSIFIED: The boundary rule's genes match the element's cell type more often than genes at a matched distance ({cc}%, one-sided p {p}), so position carries cell-type information here.
outcome_wording.FALSIFIED: The boundary rule's genes match the element's cell type no more often than genes at a matched distance ({cc}%, one-sided p {p}): on this endpoint the boundary rule carries no cell-type information beyond distance, and it is falsified as a carrier of it.
outcome_wording.rotation_ahead: With the same boundaries rotated along each arm the rule averages {rm}% on these elements, below the measured boundaries' (one-sided p {pr}), so where the boundaries lie, not only how many there are, carries information here.
outcome_wording.rotation_not_ahead: With the same boundaries rotated along each arm the rule averages {rm}% on these elements (one-sided p {pr}), so the measured positions are not shown to carry more than the boundaries' number and spacing.
outcome_wording.all_distal: On all {N} distal elements (beside, deciding nothing; the rules differ on {kA}) the boundary rule is concordant for {kbA} ({cbA}%) against {knA} ({cnA}%) for nearest TSS, {dA} points [{loA}, {hiA}], and against {kgA} ({cgA}%) for the gene-structure rule, {dgA} points [{logA}, {higA}].
outcome_wording.missing: {miss} of the attributed genes on this population are absent from the RNA atlas's rows and are counted as not concordant.
outcome_wording.tail: Accessibility is not function, and a boundary is not a regulatory unit by itself: this says the attributed gene is expressed where the element is open, not that the element acts on it. The boundaries come from 2-3 h embryos while the elements and the RNA come from larval-to-adult brain, a wider stage gap than section 9's; accessibility and RNA come from different nuclei and different studies; and the element source states no licence.

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 7aef5af

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
